easy.q: What was Elder Soares’s talk mainly about?
options: Getting ready to serve a mission
Living the law of the fast in a holier way
Learning the stories of the pioneers
easy.why: Elder Soares testified of the power that comes “as we seek to live this law in a higher and holier way.” The law he meant is the law of the fast.

easy.q: Before the Savior began His ministry, where did He go to fast and pray?
options: Into the wilderness
Onto a ship at sea
Up to a king’s palace
easy.why: Elder Soares said the Savior “withdrew into the wilderness and spent 40 days communing with His Father.”

easy.q: In the promise Elder Soares read from Isaiah, what does the Lord say when we cry to Him?
options: “Be still”
“Fear not”
“Here I am”
easy.why: Isaiah’s promise is “thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am.” Elder Soares called it a tender promise that the Lord is near.

easy.q: In our day, what did Elder Soares say we give to help people in need when we fast?
options: Handwritten letters
Generous fast offerings
Baskets of garden food
easy.why: Elder Soares taught that our desire to help others “finds tangible expression in generous fast offerings.”

easy.q: What did Elder Soares invite us to prayerfully ponder?
options: The psalms of King David
The journeys of Paul
Isaiah’s teachings on the fast
easy.why: He said, “I invite you to prayerfully ponder Isaiah’s teachings” and to embrace the purpose of the law of the fast in a higher and holier way.

medium.q: According to Elder Soares, what did the Lord do for His covenant people in Isaiah chapter 58?
options: Set how many hours a proper fast should last
Lifted their vision beyond outward observance of the fast
Released them from fasting in times of hardship
Taught that fasting matters more than prayer
medium.why: Elder Soares said the Lord “lifted the vision of His covenant people beyond the outward observance of this law” and revealed fasting as an act of worship.

medium.q: Elder Soares said that of all the Savior could have done to prepare for His mission, He chose to fast and pray. What was the Savior seeking?
options: Followers who would become His first disciples
A sign that His ministry should begin
Complete alignment with His Father’s will
Rest before the hard labors ahead of Him
medium.why: Elder Soares taught that the Savior “chose to seek complete alignment with His Father’s will through earnest fasting and prayer.”

medium.q: According to Elder Soares, what happens to us through the union of fasting and prayer?
options: We grow more humble and aware of our dependence on the Lord
We grow more able to rely on our own strength
We earn the particular answers we most hope for
We find we need to pray less often than before
medium.why: He taught that through fasting joined with prayer, we “become more humble and more aware of our complete dependence upon the Lord.”

medium.q: Why did Elder Soares quote the Prophet Joseph Smith about a man “filled with the love of God”?
options: To show that fasting is first a duty of Church leaders
To show that blessing our own family is enough
To show that fasting replaces other kinds of service
To show that our fast should turn our hearts toward others
medium.why: The quotation says such a person “is not content with blessing his family alone.” Elder Soares used it to teach that our fast is also an outward expression of charity.

medium.q: How did Elder Soares connect generous fast offerings to the Savior?
options: The Savior paid offerings at the temple
The Savior fed thousands with loaves and fishes
The Savior came and suffered so He could succor His people
The Savior praised a widow who gave two mites
medium.why: Elder Soares said this generosity “reflects the Savior’s own example,” who came down from heaven and suffered so He would know how to succor His people.

hard.q: Elder Soares said this pattern of fasting is more than a test of restraint or a petition for specific blessings. What did he say it is?
options: A proof of how strong our self-discipline has become
An elevating expression of faith and trust in the Lord
A way to qualify for the blessing we are asking for
A duty we keep chiefly by going without food
hard.why: He called it “an elevating expression of faith and trust in the Lord,” a way to align our desires with His purposes and our expectations with His wisdom.

hard.q: Someone fasts and prays about a heavy trial, and the trial remains. Which response best fits what Elder Soares taught from the Savior’s example?
options: The fast must be repeated until the trial is taken away
The fast shows the request was not the Lord’s concern
The fast was likely not sincere enough to be accepted
The fast still draws heaven near and gives power to endure
hard.why: Elder Soares said fasting and prayer “may not remove every burden from our path,” but they draw heaven near and give divine power to overcome or endure.

hard.q: Elder Soares said we give fast offerings not only for the benefit of those in need. What else did he say generous giving expresses?
options: Our love for the Lord and commitment to His work
Our thanks for the prosperity we have enjoyed
Our hope of being blessed with greater means
Our wish to be counted among the faithful
hard.why: He taught that we give “as an expression of our love for the Lord and our commitment to His work,” consecrating both our means and our time to Him.

hard.q: From what he has personally witnessed, how did Elder Soares say the blessings of fasting often enter people’s lives?
options: Suddenly and unmistakably
Quietly and tenderly
Only after many years
Mostly in material ways
hard.why: Elder Soares said the blessings of fasting often come “quietly and tenderly,” softening hearts, strengthening testimonies, and transforming lives.

hard.q: Elder Soares quoted President Joseph F. Smith on proper fasting. According to that quotation, how does fasting promote communion with the Holy Ghost?
options: By freeing more hours for gospel study
By proving to the Lord that we will sacrifice
By placing the body in subjection to the spirit
By setting us apart from worldly company
hard.why: President Joseph F. Smith, as Elder Soares quoted him, taught that proper fasting would “place the body in subjection to the spirit” and bring us nearer to God.
